newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai firms, instruments placed on CreditAlert-TRIS.
newsitem.headline: Thai firms, instruments placed on CreditAlert-TRIS.

text.p: The Thai Rating and Information Services agency said on Thursday that it had placed all Thai firms and debt instruments rated by it on CreditAlert with "negative" implication following the authorities decision to float the baht.

TRIS said in a statement that the baht flotation on Wednesday, which was a virtual and deliberate devaluation of the currency, would negatively affect the companies by increasing their foreign exchange lossses and debt servicing burdens.

CreditAlert as part of TRIS's monitoring process is a public warning when there is insufficient information to fully assess and reconsider a debt instrument's current rating or when significant events may affect a company's rating already assigned by the agency because of changing business conditions.
Existing ratings of firms or debt instruments would continue unchanged for the present, TRIS said. Monitoring would be done until a debt instrument matures or the company's rating contract expires.
It added that as of end-1996, outstanding external debts were $16.80 billion for the government, $13.91 billion for state enterprises and $62.28 billion for the private sector.

"In addition, the higher cost of imported capital goods and raw materials will likely push up the operating costs of those rated companies and restrict demands for their products in the short and medium term," the agency said.
TRIS said it will monitor closely these effects on the business environment particularly those issuers with substantial non-baht exposure in revising their ratings.
